## A systematic review of laxative use in critically unwell patients: Are we doing more harm than good?

:::: {.justify}

Diarrhoea is common in critically unwell patients and is associated with prolonged intensive care unit (ICU) stay and increased mortality. Its causes are multifactorial; however, emerging evidence suggests that laxative exposure may be an important, and potentially modifiable, contributor. Laxatives are frequently prescribed in ICU patients to prevent constipation, increasingly as part of bowel management protocols (BMP) and care bundles, despite limited supporting evidence. This systematic review evaluated the effects and prevailing associations of laxatives on clinical outcomes in critically unwell adults.

[Read the full paper](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/17511437261487004)
